nodes.description: Splicing-modulating variants reduce the functional full-length transcript to roughly half. Which exon they act on varies, and the dosage reduction rather than any one exon is the general mechanism: the classic alleles of both neurological presentations raise a minor isoform lacking the exon-4-encoded residues, while c.168+6T>A acts on exon 2 and the 2025 series reports exon 5 skipping, exon 8 skipping and a pseudoexon insertion. The resulting short isoforms are inert in the complex rather than toxic to it, so the pathogenic unit is the missing quantity of normal protein.
nodes.id: Aberrant Splicing and Reduced Full-Length Transcript

nodes.description: A partial-loss X-linked allele. Every pathogenic allele reported in this disease is a hypomorph rather than a null, and the class of allele sets which presentation follows. This entry does not assert a population-genetic reason for that, because no source cited here measures ATP6AP2 constraint; the claim is about the reported allele spectrum.

ATP6AP2 acts with ATP6AP1 in the endoplasmic reticulum, before the pump reaches its destination compartment, and its C-terminal ER-retrieval motif is required for that function while proteolytic cleavage is not. Reduced adaptor availability leaves the V0 sector incompletely assembled.

nodes.description: Under-acidification of the Golgi impairs glycosylation of other proteins. ATP6AP2 itself carries no N-glycosylation sequon, so this is not a defect in glycosylating ATP6AP2 but in the glycosylation machinery the pump supports, with its glycosylated V0 partner ATP6AP1 among the affected proteins. The abnormality is detectable in patients with purely neurological disease, not only in the hepatic presentation.
